text.p: The government on Tuesday approved the conceptual basis for a reform of the pension system, based on the system used in most Western countries.
As under the present system, a first pillar would leave pensions being paid from the collection of social tax, said Ardo Hansson, economic advisor to Prime Minister Mart Siimann.

A second pillar, to be implemented in 2000-2001, involves an insurance system for employed persons. Their future contributions, collected through an obligatory tax, will be based on the payments made into pension funds.
Also a voluntary additional insurance will be made available for those who would like to have a higher future pension. People can invest money with a tax advantage in pension funds.
The government plans to launch the first and third pillars from 1998.
"The goal is to raise the interest to pay social tax and take the whole system onto the principle of insurance, with a clear relationship between revenues and spending," he added.
Estonia has lagged behind in pension reform compared to other Central and Eastern European countries, he said.
"If the present system goes on...we are facing a very difficult choice, whether to raise taxes...or reduce the pension level," Hansson said.
